title: Modernize performance sandbox, CI gateways, and dependency upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The current performance test harness has accreted multiple ad-hoc scripts, env-var driven configs, and two different runners (legacy local runner + ad-hoc container job). This makes it hard to run consistent perf regressions, reproduce CI flakes, and onboard new scenarios. We need a pragmatic refactor that reduces cognitive overhead, upgrades brittle dependencies, and gives clear CI gates for perf regressions without increasing cost of test runs.

Goals: 
- Replace the 'scripts attic' with a lightweight 'perf-sandbox' micro-runner that standardizes scenario lifecycle (prepare -> load -> validate -> artifactize).
- Introduce a small, documented scenario DSL (YAML) to express user distributions, sequence lengths, and KV-cache priming steps.
- Upgrade core dependencies (Locust -> 2.8, pytest -> 8.2, requests/urllib3 security patches) and remove an internal fork of the load harness.
- Integrate perf regression gates into GitHub Actions matrix and a low-cost nightly job that runs heavy scenarios on dedicated runners.
- Provide deterministic artifacts: consolidated CSV/Parquet traces per run + normalized latency histograms for p50/p95/p99.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Chosen approach: best-effort compatibility with existing scenario definitions; we will provide a compatibility shim that rewrites legacy JSON scenarios into the new DSL. This keeps rollout incremental and avoids blocking dependent teams.
- We prefer keeping the runner lightweight (Python) rather than moving to a full Go rewrite to reduce time-to-delivery. Longer-term we may revisit a compiled runner if throughput cost becomes dominant.
- CI integration: use self-hosted GHA runners that have GPU/CPU labels; keep heavy (multi-hour) scenarios scheduled nightly to avoid burn on PRs. PR-level smoke should run small sub-scenarios with mocked KV priming.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) perf-sandbox can run all existing canonical scenarios through compatibility shim with <= 5% variance versus legacy harness on same machine.
2) CI: PR-level smoke runs in GHA < 20 minutes; nightly full suite runs report artifacts in S3 and create a dashboard entry.
3) Dependency upgrades complete with a clear migration doc; no regressions introduced to device-facing runtime (verified by rolling job on staging).
4) New DSL and runner documented with examples; onboarding doc for platform and solutions teams.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): build perf-sandbox, DSL, compatibility shim, and small PR smoke integration.
- Phase 2 (follow-up): enable nightly full suite, add dashboard ingestion, tune runner resource limits.
- Phase 3: deprecate legacy harness scripts after 2 weeks of parallel runs and zero-release regressions.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Number of flaky CI runs per week (target: reduce flakiness by 60%).
- Time to reproduce a perf regression locally (target: < 30 minutes).
- Nightly suite runtime and cost (target: keep within current spend +10%).
